name: Customer satisfaction
definition: Survey-based customer experience score. Higher scores indicate better experience.
note: C-MeX has no fixed numeric company target. The current peer comparison uses the 2024/25 sector median. Ofwat shows 74.43; the original APR shows 74.42. Only the final-year median is shown in this version; no five-year target score is calculated.

name: Priority services reach
definition: Share of households on the priority services register. Reach is one of three PSR components.
note: A lower reach than the sector is an investigation prompt, not proof of inadequate support. Customer needs vary. Ofwat states the overall PSR commitment was met in 2024/25; the five-year calculation here covers reach only.

name: Leakage reduction
definition: Reduction in three-year average leakage from the 2019/20 baseline. Negative reduction means leakage increased.
note: Comparison is of percentage reduction, not absolute leakage efficiency. Ofwat reports signed change; this project reverses its sign so positive means reduction. Historical percentage targets are unchanged in the revised 2023 APR; no original volume target is mixed with restated volumes.

name: Per capita consumption
definition: Household water consumption per person, measured as a three-year average.
note: The peer comparison uses unadjusted three-year averages. Ofwat also reports a COVID-adjusted value of 130.4 for payment assessment, still above the 129.0 target. The trend uses percentage reduction from baseline, with higher being better; negative values mean an increase.

name: Supply interruptions
definition: Average interruption time per property, counting supply interruptions lasting over three hours.
note: The stored values and chart axis are seconds per property; headline durations are also shown as minutes and seconds. Actuals use the 2025 APR historical summary, which includes restatements. The 2023 APR describes a 24-second methodological reduction for 2022/23, so the full change should not be attributed solely to operational improvement.

name: Drinking water quality
definition: Compliance Risk Index combines the significance of drinking-water failures and regulatory response. It is not a percentage of unsafe water.
note: The full target is 0.00; the payment deadband is 2.00. The APR reports 1.53 for calendar 2020: above the full target but within the deadband. Calendar 2021–2024 are outside it. Calendar years 2020–2024 are reported in financial years 2020/21–2024/25. We retain the APR baseline and do not mix in the conflicting 3.94 value under the Ofwat baseline heading.

name: Unplanned outage
definition: Temporary unplanned loss of water production capacity.

name: Mains repairs
definition: Repairs to burst or leaking mains, normalised by network length. Fewer failures is better.

name: Internal sewer flooding
definition: Internal sewer flooding incidents normalised by sewer connections.
note: Original APR history is 1.89, 1.63, 1.68, 1.69, 1.33. Ofwat October 2025 reports 1.52 for the last year. Both versions are visible. A harmonised five-year achievement score and change rate are withheld until the full history is reconciled. Annual statuses in the overview matrix refer only to the original APR.

name: Pollution incidents
definition: Category 1–3 pollution incidents normalised by sewer length. Distinct from storm-overflow spill counts.
note: Calendar years 2020–2024 align to reporting years 2020/21–2024/25. Annual company data do not establish incident causes or forecast future spills.

name: Treatment works compliance
definition: Proportion of treatment works meeting numeric discharge-permit conditions.
note: The full target is 100%; 99% is a payment deadband, not the target. Ofwat assesses this measure against the deadband for its overall categorisation. The five-year full-target score is calculated from numeric actuals; the APR has an inconsistent Yes flag in 2022/23 despite 99.33%.

name: Sewer collapses
definition: Sewer collapses not proactively identified that caused customer or environmental impacts.
note: The gap to the published sector average is only 0.02 collapses per 1,000 km. Treat this as a small comparative gap, not a major failure.
